text:
marco: Hey team — planning to enable new catalog entry falcon-retro-1.4 across hosted and dedicated. Proposing a staggered rollout + explicit fallback ordering. Change window target: 02:00-05:00 UTC tomorrow. Canaries: 2% US-EAST, 2% EU-WEST. Need signoff on abort criteria and enterprise pin strategy.
sarah: quick q — what are our abort thresholds? p95 latency % increase? error spike? quality regressions?
marco: good call. abort if: p95 latency > baseline + 20% for >5m, error rate >0.5% sustained 3m, or eval quality drop >3% on prompt-set A. Also abort if token cost increases >15% and no quality upside.
release-coordinator: noted — change window reserved 02:00-05:00 UTC (tz: UTC). Canary targets set. Adding rollout task to release board.
deploy-bot: start_rollout: model=falcon-retro-1.4 stage=canary regions=[us-east-1, eu-west-1] percent=2
deploy-bot: pods_created=18, routes_updated=2, cache_warm=true
lee: For fallback order I propose: 1) falcon-retro-1.4 (primary) 2) falcon-retro-1.3-quant (low-memory) 3) redwood-compat-v1 (stable fallback) 4) model-legacy-embed (last resort). Keeps lower-cost quantized variant before hitting older baseline. Thoughts?
olivia: +1 on ordering. Also: some enterprise customers (ACME, FinCo) need pinning to current stable for 48h post-rollout. We should add a per-customer routing rule. Example snippet: ```json
{"route": "customer:ACME", "model_pin": "falcon-retro-1.3", "until": "2026-03-25T00:00:00Z"}
```
marco: thanks. I’ll add a rollout step to create pins for flagged enterprise tenants before expanding % beyond canary. Also adding a guard: bump canary only if QA smoke passes and no abort triggers.
sarah: monitoring checklist: p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, completions-per-request drift, token-count delta, user-facing quality evals. Can we wire an automatic alert to #eng-oncall for p95 breach?
marco: yes — will add Grafana alert and a PagerDuty runbook link. Also enabling a short quality eval harness against prompt-set A every 10 minutes during canary.
deploy-bot: canary metrics t+12m: requests=9,120, p50=83ms (baseline 75ms), p95=320ms (baseline 265ms), 5xx_rate=0.12%, token_delta=+7%
deploy-bot: quality-harness: pass_rate=98.6% (baseline 99.1%)
sarah: p95 up ~20% relative to baseline. It's borderline but within abort threshold if sustained. Any idea if KV cache hit rate changed?
marco: cache hit was down ~6% in us-east due to model tokenization differences. Plan: increase prefix cache TTL by 30s and enable hot-cache warming for top-100 prompts. That should bring p95 down.
lee: agree. Also consider routing heavy requesters to quant variant during next expansion to 25% to reduce tail latency.
olivia: I've created the enterprise pin tasks and notified acct owners. They asked for a 48h pin window; added to rollout plan.
release-coordinator: updated rollout timeline: canary now -> 02:00–02:30 UTC verify -> 02:30 expand to 25% -> 03:30 expand to 60% if stable -> 04:30 full. Enterprise pins applied before 02:30.
marco: if metrics hold or improve after cache tweak, proceed to 25% at 02:30. If not, rollback to falcon-retro-1.3-quant and open a bug for tokenization regressions.
deploy-bot: metrics t+40m after TTL bump: p95=280ms, 5xx_rate=0.08%, quality-harness=99.0% — within targets. Proceeding as approved to 25% at 02:30 unless manual stop. :thumbsup:
sarah: good. I'll watch the dashboard and escalate if anything drifts.
marco: thanks all. leaving the thread open until full rollout or rollback. I’ll post final status when complete.
